overview: Clients send resumable chunked uploads to an upload service that writes chunks to object storage and records them in metadata. Devices long-poll a changes endpoint for sync. Conflicts are resolved by keeping both versions.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative file: 100 MB; 4 MB blocks; one changed block.
estimation.calculation: ceil(100 / 4) = 25 blocks; delta upload = 4 MB instead of 100 MB.
estimation.result: A one-block edit transfers about 4% of the original file size.
estimation.implication: Immutable chunking reduces transfer cost; metadata needs atomic version and block-list updates.

components.purpose: Mobile caller with intermittent connectivity for dropbox / google drive.
components.rationale: Use stable request IDs and reconnect/cursor recovery rather than assuming one continuous session.

components.purpose: Authenticate, apply admission limits and route requests for dropbox / google drive.
components.rationale: Keep business invariants in the owning service; reject malformed or excessive traffic before expensive work.

components.purpose: Resumable chunked upload; SHA-1 per chunk for dedup
components.rationale: Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

components.purpose: Long-poll /changes; conflicting edits keep both versions
components.rationale: Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

components.purpose: Persist immutable large objects for dropbox / google drive.
components.rationale: Publish metadata pointers only after objects are complete; use checksums, versioned keys and lifecycle cleanup.

components.purpose: Store documents and their versioned lifecycle for dropbox / google drive.
components.rationale: Index the access keys and use conditional updates for state changes; avoid unbounded embedded histories.

entityDetails.purpose: Atomic metadata version pointing to an immutable block list.
accessPatterns: Commit a version with an expected previous version; list changes after a cursor.
constraints: Compare-and-swap version prevents lost updates; keep both versions or surface a conflict.
relationships: block_hashes reference immutable Block objects in file order; commit the complete list atomically.

entityDetails.purpose: Immutable file bytes stored independently from metadata.
accessPatterns: Upload missing blocks; fetch a file version by ordered block list.
constraints: Validate checksum and ownership; content dedup must not expose other users' data.
relationships: FileVersion references content hashes; block reads must still enforce file ownership.

apiDetails.rationale: Presigned mode returns signed object-store URLs; upload-service mode returns service chunk URLs.

apiDetails.purpose: Upload or resume one immutable chunk.
apiDetails.rationale: Retry the same chunk number and checksum safely; metadata commit is a separate operation.

apiDetails.purpose: Publish a new file version after all referenced blocks exist.
apiDetails.rationale: Commit the version and change cursor atomically; incomplete blocks must not become a visible file.

apiDetails.purpose: Sync file changes to another device.
apiDetails.rationale: A durable cursor recovers missed WebSocket hints or long-poll responses.

buildSteps.title: Clients
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Mobile Client and name it “Clients”. Place it in the leftmost caller/background lane. Mobile caller with intermittent connectivity for dropbox / google drive. Use stable request IDs and reconnect/cursor recovery rather than assuming one continuous session. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Gateway
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add API Gateway and name it “Gateway”. Place it in column 2, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are Clients. Authenticate, apply admission limits and route requests for dropbox / google drive. Keep business invariants in the owning service; reject malformed or excessive traffic before expensive work. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Upload Service
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Service and name it “Upload Service”. Place it in column 3, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are Gateway. Resumable chunked upload; SHA-1 per chunk for dedup Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Sync Service
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Service and name it “Sync Service”. Place it in column 3, row 2 of the HLD; its callers are Gateway. Long-poll /changes; conflicting edits keep both versions Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Chunk storage
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Object Storage and name it “Chunk storage”. Place it in column 4, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are Upload Service. Persist immutable large objects for dropbox / google drive. Publish metadata pointers only after objects are complete; use checksums, versioned keys and lifecycle cleanup. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Metadata
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Document DB and name it “Metadata”. Place it in column 4, row 2 of the HLD; its callers are Upload Service, Sync Service. Store documents and their versioned lifecycle for dropbox / google drive. Index the access keys and use conditional updates for state changes; avoid unbounded embedded histories. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

steps.title: Clients → Gateway → Upload Service → Chunk storage
steps.explanation: Validate chunk identity and checksum, then stream bytes with bounded memory.

steps.title: Upload Service → Metadata
steps.explanation: Commit the ordered block list and new file version after all chunks exist.

steps.title: Clients → Gateway → Sync Service → Metadata
steps.explanation: Read changes after the last durable cursor; retain conflicting versions instead of silently overwriting.

failureCases.scenario: Upload succeeds but metadata commit fails
failureCases.handling: Leave uploaded blocks unreferenced, allow a retry with the same upload ID, and garbage-collect abandoned blocks after a grace period. Never expose a partial file version.

alternatives: Use presigned content-addressed blocks to bypass app-server bandwidth and support delta sync. Use an upload fleet for centralized scanning, validation and transport control at higher transfer cost.
